source.descriptionClaim: A three-and-a-half hour compilation of 13 original hacking documentaries covering state-sponsored hacking, cybercrime, and criminal hacker groups.
source.sourceScope: The available source snapshot exposes video metadata and the chapter index, not a complete verbatim transcript. Chapter-derived facts are stored as topics unless independently corroborated.

learnedPatterns: Cyber operations can be strategic instruments for espionage, coercion, disruption, sabotage, influence, and criminal profit.
Attribution is an evidence problem: actor labels, state links, motives, infrastructure, malware, victimology, and timing must remain separable claims until corroborated.
Cyber-physical incidents require modeling both digital effects and real-world operational consequences.
Counterintelligence includes hardware, supply-chain, emissions, and physical inspection concerns in addition to software telemetry.
Ransomware ecosystems separate operators, affiliates, infrastructure, access brokers, victims, monetization, and public leak/extortion surfaces.
Historical cases are useful as defensive pattern libraries, not as authorization to reproduce intrusion methods.
Third-party documentary claims must retain provenance and confidence instead of being promoted automatically to fact.
